messages:
Jane (Customer): Hey team — were seeing intermittent 500s from /v1/generate. No request-id in our server logs (we strip headers before shipping). I have a screenshot of the browser network panel. What exact bits do you need to help debug?

Maria (Support): Hi Jane — sorry about the hit. Short answer: we need a request identifier (req/ref/id) and ideally the request/response headers or a HAR. If that's hard, a screenshot is fine as long as the network row shows the request headers or the response headers. Typical headers we look for: `x-request-id`, `x-rw-reqref`, `x-server-trace`. Also, from the Console you can make a Debug Token — that links client traces to backend traces.

Devin (Eng): Quick checklist for reproducibility:
1) HAR or curl (including all request headers)
2) Server logs around the timestamp (±30s)
3) Client timestamp (UTC) and approximate region
4) Any edge/gateway headers (Cloudflare, ALB, nginx)
If you cant export a HAR, a screenshot highlighting the request + the response headers/time is usually enough.

Jane (Customer): I exported a HAR and noticed a header `x-rw-reqref: 01FJAbcDef1234`. Is that the same as the request id you need?

Maria (Support): Yes, `x-rw-reqref` is our frontend request reference — perfect. If you can paste that value here we can trace it. Also, if possible run a curl reproduction so we can see the full roundtrip. Example:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n     -H "x-rw-reqref: 01FJAbcDef1234" \\n     -d '{"input":"test"}' \\n     https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
```

If the server returns a 500, paste the response body and any response headers (we look for `x-server-trace` or `x-upstream-error`).

SRE Bot: Note: with a request ref we can query the trace store. Please include the client timestamp (UTC) and timezone to narrow the window.

Jane (Customer): One more thing — on Android our logs only show `session=...` and not an obvious req-id. Where should I look in the SDK?

Devin (Eng): Android SDK maps the outgoing header to `X-Req-Ref` and logs it under `reqRef` in debug logging. On React Native / webview youll see `x-rw-reqref` in the network tab. iOS (URLSession) exposes `X-Request-Id` in the response headers. If your proxy strips headers, check the proxy logs for `x-amzn-trace-id` or `x-cf-request-id` — those sometimes carry the original ID.

Maria (Support): If you cant extract headers, we can still create a debug bundle from the Console: Console -> Requests -> find by time -> Download debug bundle (zip). Or from the SDK call `Redwood.createDebugToken()` and paste the token here. The token looks like `dbg_tok_<alnum>` and lets us pull client-side traces.

Jane (Customer): Ok I ran the curl and got a 500. Response body: `{"error":"internal"}`. Response headers included `x-server-trace: trace-9a3b` and `x-rw-reqref: 01FJAbcDef1234`. I also generated a debug token: dbg_tok_202390XYZ (redacted). Sending HAR + token now.

Maria (Support): Got both — thanks. Well correlate `01FJAbcDef1234` with the trace `trace-9a3b` and come back with the service span and root cause. FYI — if your traffic goes through Cloudflare/ALB, include `x-cf-request-id` or `x-amzn-trace-id` too; those help when headers are rewritten.

Devin (Eng): One tip for future captures: in Chrome devtools Network panel right-click the request -> Save as HAR with content. That preserves headers and response bodies. If doing command-line repros, add `-v` to curl so you get the raw response headers printed.

Jane (Customer): Thanks! Attaching HAR + curl output + debug token. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

Maria (Support): Well update this thread with the trace links and next steps once we finish the correlation.
